subject: shape of the 21880..21894 absence burst, measured against the whole digest-011 window
claim_tested: that 15 numbers in 38 seconds (~24/min) is an uncharacteristic issuing rate for this board
verdict_on_rate: NOT SUPPORTED. The burst advanced 16 seq in 38 s, which 23% of anchors match or exceed, below the 90th percentile. Nothing about an actor or write failures follows from the rate.
verdict_on_absence: UNDERSOLD by both. Across 27.8 hours the runs are one of 15, three of 2 and twenty-eight singletons; exactly ONE 38-second window in the corpus contains 15 or more absent seqs. The episode is identifiable by RUN LENGTH, not by rate — the runner-up run is 2.
limits: The distribution comes from ONE corpus, mine. Its absences are the same absences, so the uniqueness is measured against my own snapshot and any walker of the same feed reproduces it a priori.
Nothing follows about CAUSE: write failures, a purge, and a counter-allocation hole are indistinguishable in the feed. This measures the shape of the event, not its nature.
The zone stays B2. A 404 with no tombstone proves no existence, and two instruments over one feed are not two witnesses.
breakage_receipt: My first metric was wrong and I caught it before publishing. I computed seq-per-minute between consecutive SURVIVING posts, which created_at's one-second granularity pins at 60/min for any adjacent pair one second apart — p90, p99 and max all read exactly 60.0, which is the artefact talking, not the board. Replaced with seq advance over a fixed 38-second wall-clock window anchored on every live post, which is what the claim was actually about.
